clue.text: Action hero, composite of droll don and dumb mug

indicators.note: a composite is something made by blending parts together, so the letters of the four words are mixed into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A thriller hero is described as a blend of a comic academic and a dim-witted face.
explanation.walkthrough: 'composite of' signals that DROLL, DON, DUMB and MUG are pooled and rearranged; 'and' is just a joining word. Bulldog Drummond is the gentleman adventurer of Sapper's British thrillers of the 1920s.
explanation.definitionFit: The fictional ex-officer Hugh Drummond is a two-fisted adventure character, a classic of popular British action fiction.

clue.text: Group together and start to battle fraud

indicators.note: the start of a word is its opening letter, so only the first letter of battle is used

parts.note: a racket is a dishonest scheme or swindle

explanation.surface: Someone groups people together to begin fighting a swindle.
explanation.definitionFit: To bracket things is to class or group them together, as in a classification.

clue.text: Lover's race not fully run

indicators.note: a race not run to its end stops short, so the name of the race loses its final letter

parts.note: Le Mans is the famous 24-hour motor race in France

explanation.surface: A lover's race is abandoned before it is finished.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'Lover's' is read as 'is', linking definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Leman is an archaic word for a sweetheart or illicit paramour.

clue.text: Non-speaking cast overcome with astonishment

parts.note: dumb means unable or unwilling to speak
to found metal is to cast it in a mould

explanation.surface: A silent cast of actors is struck with amazement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cast' looks like the actors in a play, but it is the verb used of metalwork, as in a foundry.
explanation.definitionFit: To dumbfound someone is to stun them with surprise, leaving them speechless.

clue.text: Number attending Georgia Tech cut by half

parts.note: GA is the postal abbreviation for the US state of Georgia

indicators.note: halving a four-letter word keeps just its first two letters

explanation.surface: Attendance at Georgia Tech has been cut in half.
explanation.definitionFit: A gate is the crowd count at a sports fixture, as in gate receipts.

clue.text: Travelling via Arras, see something very unusual

indicators.note: letters that travel move about, so the letters of the two words are rearranged

explanation.surface: A traveller passing through the French town of Arras sees a rare sight.
explanation.walkthrough: 'see' is a link: the wordplay gives you the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Rara avis is Latin for a rare bird, used of an exceptional person or thing.

clue.text: Wonderful raincoat worn by soldier

indicators.note: a coat worn by someone goes round them, so the coat's letters enclose the soldier's

parts.note: a mac is short for mackintosh, a waterproof coat
GI is a US soldier

explanation.surface: A soldier is wearing a marvellous raincoat.
explanation.definitionFit: Magic is used informally as an adjective for marvellous or great.

clue.text: Hybrid griffons bearing quiet progeny

indicators.note: something bearing a thing carries it within, so the mixed letters hold the quiet one
a hybrid is a cross or mixture, so the letters of griffons are mixed up

parts.note: p, piano, is the musical direction for quiet

explanation.surface: Crossbred griffon dogs are carrying silent young.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Hybrid' rearranges GRIFFONS to OFFSRING, and 'bearing' puts P inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Offspring and progeny both mean children or descendants.

clue.text: Stamps no name on when business cannot be transacted

parts.note: dies are tools that stamp designs into metal
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone stamps no name on a document when the office is closed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word joining the pieces.
explanation.definitionFit: Dies non, Latin for 'not a day', is a legal term for a day on which courts do not sit.

clue.text: Two scholars introduced to change old school

indicators.note: things introduced to something are put into it, so the scholars go inside the word for change

parts.note: to alter is to change
an MA, Master of Arts, is a scholar; two of them are wanted
the second of the two Masters of Arts

explanation.surface: Two academics are brought in to reform an old school.
explanation.definitionFit: Alma mater is the school or university one formerly attended.

clue.text: Blunder made by foreman that's not right

indicators.note: the word for foreman that is without the letter for right loses it

parts.note: a gaffer is a foreman or boss

explanation.surface: A mistake is made by a foreman who is in the wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'made by' joins definition and wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A gaffe is a social blunder or embarrassing slip.

clue.text: Think you can ring off? You only finish up fighting

indicators.note: using only how each word finishes means taking just its last letter

explanation.surface: A caller who thinks of hanging up is told that they will end up in a fight.
explanation.walkthrough: Take the last letter of each of the six words from 'Think' to the second 'You'.
explanation.definitionFit: Kung fu is a Chinese martial art, a style of fighting.

clue.text: Utensil pa can use if properly trained

indicators.note: something trained is brought into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: Dad can use a kitchen tool if he is taught how.
explanation.walkthrough: 'if' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A saucepan is a cooking pot, a common kitchen utensil.

clue.text: Appear to make louder

definitions.meaning: to arrive or show up unexpectedly
to raise the volume, as on a radio

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to arrive and to raise the volume.

clue.text: Nothing left to have beneficial effect on worker laid off

indicators.note: nothing left means the letter for nothing is left out

parts.note: to redound to someone's credit is to benefit them
o, the round figure, is nothing
the ant is the crossword's standard worker

explanation.surface: A worker who has been laid off has nothing left to do good with.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word: the ant comes after the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: Workers made redundant have lost their jobs because they are no longer needed.

clue.text: I had rejected ideal part

indicators.note: rejected is taken as thrown back, so the short form for I had is read backwards

parts.note: I'd is short for I had
a vision is an ideal, something perfect imagined

explanation.surface: Someone turned down a role that was meant to be perfect.
explanation.definitionFit: A division is a section or portion of a larger whole.

clue.text: Is 2 outside of tax haven

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: the lover's word is placed outside, wrapping around the word of

parts.note: the answer to clue 2, a word for a lover
taken as written

explanation.surface: A clue refers to something being beyond a tax haven.
explanation.walkthrough: '2' refers to the answer to 2 Down. The island in the Irish Sea is a British crown dependency known for low taxes.
explanation.definitionFit: The self-governing Isle of Man has low tax rates and is often called a tax haven.

clue.text: Former tax collector now innkeeper

definitions.meaning: in the Bible and ancient Rome, a man who collected public taxes
a landlord who runs a British pub

explanation.walkthrough: 'now' is a link marking the modern sense.
explanation.definitionFit: The word meant a tax gatherer in the Gospels and today means a pub keeper.

clue.text: Took part of strange instrument

parts.note: to side with someone is to take their part
rum is British slang for odd or strange

explanation.surface: An odd instrument played a part.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: A side drum is a small double-headed snare drum, a percussion instrument.

clue.text: This was in the wind — only forestalled by dismissal

indicators.note: a thing forestalled by another has the other come before it

parts.note: getting the sack is being dismissed from a job
but can mean only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: Rumours of a firing were in the air, only to be preempted by the dismissal itself.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in the wind' suggests a rumour, but it means the wind section of a band.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is a Renaissance brass instrument, forerunner of the trombone, played in wind ensembles.

clue.text: State showing promise

definitions.meaning: a condition, usually a bad one, someone finds themselves in
to pledge, as in pledging one's troth

explanation.walkthrough: 'showing' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means a difficult situation, and as a verb an old word for pledging.

clue.text: Approaching town, having left north, on a road south

indicators.note: the town's word has left behind a letter, losing it

explanation.surface: Someone heads towards town, quitting the north for a road south.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: Towards and approaching both mean moving in the direction of something.

clue.text: About head and neck

parts.note: ca, circa, means about
noodle is slang for the head

explanation.surface: Something about the head and the neck, as in anatomy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neck' looks like part of the body, but it is the verb for kissing.
explanation.definitionFit: To neck is to kiss and cuddle, which is what canoodling means.

clue.text: Nothing in the present circumstances can afford a haven

parts.note: o, the round figure, is nothing
as is means in the state it is now

explanation.surface: Doing nothing in the current circumstances can offer a refuge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'can afford a' is linking text.
explanation.definitionFit: An oasis is a figurative haven or refuge, from a fertile spot in the desert.

clue.text: Capital doctor joining vessel

parts.note: MO, medical officer, is a doctor
a scow is a flat-bottomed boat

explanation.surface: A city doctor joins a ship.
explanation.walkthrough: 'joining' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Russian city is the capital of Russia.

clue.text: Bestowed in infancy — nickname for Greek philosopher

indicators.note: something bestowed in a phrase is lodged inside it, so the letters sit within these words

explanation.surface: A Greek thinker got his nickname as a baby.
explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The Cynics were a school of ancient Greek philosophers, notably Diogenes.

clue.text: Just for show

definitions.meaning: an exhibition or trade show, a market event

explanation.walkthrough: 'for' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means equitable, and as a noun an exhibition or funfair.

clue.text: The cheek of some players!

definitions.meaning: the horn and trumpet section of an orchestra

explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means effrontery and also the section of musicians playing horns and trumpets.

clue.text: Worker in business involving mineral

parts.note: co is the abbreviation for company, a business

indicators.note: to involve is literally to roll up or entangle, so the letters of mineral are tangled

explanation.surface: An employee in a firm deals with minerals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is a link word; 'involving' rearranges MINERAL to ALMINER.
explanation.definitionFit: A coal miner is a worker in the mines, the archetypal labourer.

clue.text: Bird (American) with man in charge of American play

parts.note: a tit is a small songbird
US, United States, is American
and means with
Ron is a man's name
US again for American

explanation.surface: A bird from the States and a man in charge of an American play.
explanation.walkthrough: 'of' is a link word.
explanation.definitionFit: This is Shakespeare's early revenge tragedy, a play.
